clue.text: Advances with pamphlet one deducts

indicators.note: read as 'having within', so the pamphlet word sits inside the advances word

parts.note: subs are advances of money, as on wages
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious

explanation.surface: Someone takes money advanced along with a leaflet, and one person does the deducting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' reads as 'having within', an unusual container signal. 'one' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduct is to take away an amount, which is what subtracting does.

clue.text: Exact betting Eric loses heart if in charge

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the odds in horse-race betting

indicators.note: the name drops its central letters, its heart

parts.note: a man's name, here losing its middle

explanation.surface: Precise detail about a gambler called Eric who loses his nerve when put in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' removes RI, the middle pair of ERIC, leaving EC. SP (starting price) is a British betting term.
explanation.definitionFit: Specific and exact are synonyms: both mean precise and particular.

clue.text: Cabaret I find is full of germs

indicators.note: the letters are sought out and found in a new order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A nightclub act turns out to be teeming with infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'find' is a loose anagram signal: rearrange CABARET plus I. 'is full of' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are microbes, the everyday sense of germs.

clue.text: Old country loses its head for another

indicators.note: the word drops its first letter, its head

parts.note: Prussia was a former German kingdom and state

explanation.surface: A vanished nation is beheaded and swapped for a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses its head' takes P from PRUSSIA. 'another' is the definition: the result is a different country.
explanation.definitionFit: The result is a different nation from the first, so 'another' country.

clue.text: Move to protect the king shy of the French

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as is to cast
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A chess move guarding the king, though a little wary of the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' looks like an adjective but is the verb to throw. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Castling is the chess manoeuvre in which the king shelters behind a rook.

clue.text: Way park keeper is odder

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
a ranger looks after a park or forest

explanation.surface: The warden on the road through the park is rather peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranger is the comparative of strange, meaning more unusual or odder.

clue.text: Due to fly round first

indicators.note: tells us the round letter comes before the fly word

parts.note: O is round in shape
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: Something is scheduled to take to the air after first circling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts O ahead of WING. 'to' links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owing is outstanding, that is, due to be paid.

clue.text: Top of the bills in force

definitions.text: Top of the bills in force

parts.words: Top of the bills in force
parts.note: the Old Bill is British slang for the police, so the bills in a force are its constables and the top ones are their superiors

explanation.surface: Headline acts on a playbill all appear at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a theatre bill; 'the Old Bill' is British slang for the police, and those who head a force rank above the constables.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers hold rank in a police force above the ordinary constables.

clue.text: Demand is popular to pose with old bob

parts.note: something in is fashionable or popular

indicators.note: read as holding, so the coin letter goes inside the pose word

parts.note: to sit is to pose for a portrait
a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: An insistence that a fashionable person model with an old-fashioned haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a pre-decimal British shilling, abbreviated s; 'with' puts S inside SIT. 'is' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand firmly.

clue.text: Not what's called a family member

definitions.meaning: said aloud 'not' is knot, and a ... is a kind of knot so called

explanation.surface: Denying that a relative is called by that name.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition plays on 'not' sounding like knot: a granny is a badly tied reef knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny knot is a type of knot, and a granny is a grandmother, a relative.

clue.text: Alibis of old obstinate person taking English

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: the stubborn person takes in, that is holds, the letter for English

parts.note: a cuss is a cantankerous, stubborn person

explanation.surface: The stories offered by a stubborn old-timer who brings in an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is the container signal, meaning holding the English letter. Cuss as a noun for an awkward person is informal.
explanation.definitionFit: Alibis are pleas or justifications offered to avoid blame.

clue.text: Custom when I dart back turning it on

indicators.note: the two words are read from end to start
the two little words are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A habit of throwing a dart back while switching something on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns I DART into TRADI; 'turning' rearranges IT ON into TION. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a long-held practice handed down, a custom.

clue.text: Hot place to pelt bridge player with one

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's fur
North, N, is one of the four bridge positions
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: Someone throws things at a card player in a sweltering spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pelt' looks like the verb to throw at, but it is an animal's skin. Bridge players are named by compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A furnace is an enclosed chamber where intense heat is produced.

clue.text: Very much at large in a grey coat

indicators.note: the grey word wraps around the others like a coat

parts.note: taken as written
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone at liberty is dressed in a grey coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' is the container signal; 'at large' looks like one phrase meaning free, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatly means to a great degree, a large amount.

clue.text: Features of architects car is questionable

indicators.note: dubious or doubtful, so the letters are not to be trusted in this order

explanation.surface: Doubtful whether the architect's car shows those design features.
explanation.walkthrough: 'questionable' rearranges ARCHITECTS CAR IS. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Characteristics are the distinguishing traits or qualities of something.

clue.text: At first light a ludicrous act in the sea

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: an antic is a silly, grotesque act or caper

explanation.surface: At dawn, a clown does something silly in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first light' looks like one phrase meaning dawn, but splits into AT plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic is an ocean, which crosswords allow as a sea.

clue.text: Marvellous to first make mistake if nice hearted

indicators.note: just the opening letter of the preceding small word is taken

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

indicators.note: only the central letters, the heart of the word, are kept

explanation.surface: It is wonderful first to slip up, if one is kind at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to first' takes T; 'nice hearted' gives IC, the middle of NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrific in its informal sense means excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: Return of involvement

definitions.meaning: the yield earned on money invested
having a stake or concern in something

explanation.surface: The payback from getting involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest is money earned on a loan or deposit, and also a share or stake held in something.

clue.text: Covertly the faction has again lay empty

indicators.note: the faction holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a sect is a breakaway group or faction
re is a prefix meaning again

indicators.note: with its inside emptied, only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: Quietly, the splinter group has once more laid out something hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is the container signal; 'empty' strips a word to its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something covertly means in a hidden way, in private.

clue.text: Academic composed chorals

indicators.note: the letters are put together, composed afresh, in a new order

explanation.surface: A university don wrote some choir pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like writing music, but it rearranges CHORALS.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person, an academic.

clue.text: Saint Peter first is most free of risk

indicators.note: tells us the Peter word comes before the saint abbreviation

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: Saint Peter, first among apostles, is the most secure.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is old underworld slang for a safe; 'first' is the order signal that makes Peter lead even though Saint is printed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Safest is the superlative of safe, meaning the least dangerous.

clue.text: Obsession to get off the line

explanation.surface: Fixated on ending phone calls.
explanation.definitionFit: A hang-up is a fixation or complex, and to hang up is to put down the phone.

clue.text: Mechanical fleece of the ear

parts.note: to fleece someone is to rob them
otic is the medical adjective for the ear

explanation.surface: Sheep's wool from around the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' looks like wool but is the verb to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic describes something machine-like and automatic.

clue.text: Wave to the tumbler pigeon

definitions.meaning: a long swelling breaker at sea
a breed of pigeon that somersaults in flight

explanation.surface: Greeting the acrobatic bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller is a large ocean breaker and also a breed of pigeon that turns over in flight.

clue.text: Recoil from windfall with nothing

indicators.note: read as holding, so the zero goes inside the windfall word

parts.note: bunce is British slang for unexpected profit or a windfall
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone shrinks away from a lucky gain that comes to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNCE is British slang for an unexpected gain; 'with' puts O inside it. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To bounce is to spring back, to rebound or recoil.

clue.text: Number of spies in last money matters

indicators.note: the number and spies go inside the word for last

parts.note: final means last
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: How many secret agents are left when it comes to cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'of' only links. The definition is loose: an adjective standing for affairs about cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial means concerning funds, so it describes affairs about cash.

clue.text: Behold the force in robin's home the largest

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning behold

indicators.note: the force letter is placed inside the nest

parts.note: a bird such as a robin lives in a nest
g is the symbol for g-force, the force of gravity

explanation.surface: Look, the strongest bird is nesting in the biggest place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts G inside NEST. 'the' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Longest is the superlative of long, the greatest in extent or length.

clue.text: Theme to a good cold front

parts.note: taken as written
pi, short for pious, means good

indicators.note: only the leading letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: The subject of a fine cold front in the weather forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold front' looks like weather, but 'front' takes only C. Pi (pious) is a crossword word for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject or theme under discussion.

clue.text: Right, cry out lector is wrong

indicators.note: the letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Indeed, shout that the lecturer is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges CRY and LECTOR together; 'out' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Right used as an adverb means correctly, as in 'did it right'.
